newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Regional leaders seek peaceful Afghan settlement.
newsitem.headline: Regional leaders seek peaceful Afghan settlement.

text.p: The presidents of Iran and Tajikistan and ousted Afghan leader Burhanuddin Rabbani are still seeking a peaceful solution to the conflict in Afghanistan, Tajikistan's foreign minister said on Saturday.
Talbak Nazarov told reporters that the three men had discussed security issues in their volatile region when they met in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
"They agreed they should get all parties in the conflict to find a peaceful solution," he said.

The meeting was originally scheduled for Friday, but it was postponed after Rabbani's arrival was delayed. The Afghan president was forced out of Kabul last September by the purist Islamic Taleban militia.

Tajikistan, like Central Asia's other ex-Soviet republics, is concerned that the Taleban may launch a summer offensive to gain control of territory controlled by anti-Taleban forces of General Abdul Rashid Dostum and commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov has expressed fear that up to a million refugees could flood his own war-wracked country from northern Afghanistan if hostilities restarted.
Iran and Tajikistan both border Afghanistan.
